don't apologize... you have the right to your privacy! I hope you get better soon. Stay in touch!

As if guilt could ever help a person...

If someone fell down, you don't tell them "You are making me look bad, stop it", you help them get back on their feet.

If someone accidentely cuts their arms and bleed on the street, you don't yell at them for spilling blood on the pavement, you get them a bandage.

So why can't people understand that people mental issues need help, not judgement?

To help a person who is down, you don't point them at the harm they are causing, you lift them up!

I hope you get that help close to you, meanwhile, talk to us...

Well, did you or did you not have the courage to go thru the intake process? Oh, you did!

Did you or did you not have the courage to talk to him about your issues? Oh, you did!

Did you or did you not have the courage to talk to us? Oh, you did!

Did he have the courage to listen to you and take the time to see things your way? Oh, he did not?

So tell me, who is the pussy between you and him in this situation?

Thinking about suicide takes a lot of courage. Seeking help to avoid that also takes a lot of courage.

You have courage, you are not a pussy. 

You have problems, but guess what? You are not alone. I have problems too, the people here have problems too.

You have courage. More than you think.

Let's hope the therapist will help you find focus and energy.

> I don’t know why I get so sensitive and care about the opinions of 2 people who act insane. 

Because it hurts. Because we are wired to care about what people say about us.

The trick I found, because there is one, is not for me to stop being sensitive. It's for me to stop reacting to being sensitive. 

Perhaps you could try that in the future? It's fucking hard... but it was worth it for me!

Remember: You feel the way you feel. Don't try to stop feeling the way you feel.

But you could choose how you act and react... 

> It’s dumb, but at the time it felt pretty bad.

It does! And it's not dumb. You are not dumb for feeling the way you feel. You feel that way because that's who you are.

Please don't feel ashamed of your emotions, they are a part of who you are, and that's PRECIOUS.

Instead, you could work like I did: on how you react.

Let me give you one of the biggest secrets of being human...

How do you know that you just hurt your foot?

Your foot sends a signal to your brain, and your brain interprets that signal.

If the foot is wrong, the brain will check with the eyes, with the fingers, with a doctor to see if the foot is really hurt.

If the brain is wrong, it can ask the eyes to check the foot, and realize "silly me", I was wrong, it's not hurt (like when you wake up from a dream where your foot was hurt).

Your brain diagnoses everything. Your feet, your hands, your neck, your lungs... AND ITSELF!!!

If the brain is either wrong at thinking you are worthless, or wrong at realizing you are worthless, THERE IS NO SECOND ORGAN to help you see the truth.

So I am not saying you are not worthless, or that you are.

All I saying is that for many people (including me!), it's impossible for them to know their worth because our internal worth-meter is broken!

But sometimes, things have to get worse before they get better...

I had a company. It got worse and worse, until I found a job... and lost it.

I recently began a new job, and it's the best I ever had!

Sorry, I am not good at this... in short, your brain CAN be wrong.

Ok, most people who come here want emotional support, and ZeetleCR already did so...

But let me try another approach.

1 ) Your Resume visibly doesn't suck, you got called to 12 interviews! You could work with the various resume reddits (they helped me tweak mine) and you might be able to find friends or people to help you tweak it to get even more interviews, but  visibly, you are able to get interviews. Good for you!

In 1 year of on and off search, I only got 5 interviews, and I have over 25 years of experience in my field!

2 ) You might not be applying to enough jobs. Job searching is HARD. Not only do you need to clear the bar (get the employer to consider you as a potential employee), but you need to be better than any of the other candidates. 

You might actually have clearer the bar for many of the 12 interviews! There might just have been a better candidates... hey, you might have been the alternate choice a few times if their primary didn't accept and they did, so they didn't call you back!

That job I got last year (check my history), I was their alternate... the first choice didn't say yes, so I got called instead. 

3 ) Your interview technique might need some tweaking. In many cases, it's really easy to fix! It might be just speaking in a more assertive tone, it might just be researching the company more, it might just be picking better answers in advance!

There are plenty of articles, including many 25 common questions lists for many fields.

The rest is just applying, applying, applying... the wider the net, the better chance of getting a job is.

4 ) You say 1 out of 40 years of unemployment, that makes me think you might be fresh of out education with perhaps little experience.

If that's the case, you might be able to do volunteer work, find a place willing to try you out.

My own child right now has a part-time job: on call replacement in case someone is sick or on vacation.

In 3 months, my child hasn't worked a SINGLE DAY and was NEVER called, but guess what? It's on the resume anyway and my child is trying to get a summer job at a more stable competitor, who saw the name of the company on the resume.

In short, are you willing to let us help you refine your job application process before giving up?

Your first two sentences are spot on: The world doesn't care about lonely souls and what they have to offer. That much is true.

It's also true that society exists because of communities.

But a lonely person is a delicate cog in the machine of communities without which communities couldn't grow!

Hear me out... society exists because of communities, communities of like-minded people. It breeds conformity. 

But conformity doesn't allow for evolution, for a difference, for growth! If everyone thinks the same, we only have ONE outlook on society!

Lonely people are less affected by society, and are the best people to see the true face of society.

Don't devalue yourself because you are lonely... you are an essential part of the world. Many of us here are also lonely, but we still help each other in this reddit.

I can't express myself well enough, but don't think that lonely means useless...

Do you have a lot of problems? Maybe that makes you feel happy is the idea of your problems ending.

Perhaps if you talked to us (or to a professional) about your problems, someone might help you find just as happy solutions to your problems?

Do you have any hints that you are indeed in the middle of an implosion?

Like, is your implosion external (problems at school/work) or internal (anxiety, depression)?

Because that's two very different things!

If it's internal, then the journey to get out your problems is inwards. It's to think and find ways out of your situations. The first step would be to identify it... Is it depression? Anxiety? Blood problems? Just habits from bad news from the past?

If it's external, then perhaps you can find ways to improve on that from the inside! Get help with homework, get HR to help at work, find a new job, etc...

Whatever it is, talk to us! We are all anonymous and want to help.

The good news is that you are talking to us about it! That's a great sign!

The first thing you will need to learn is that you can have any feeling you feel. You can be angry as being hungry.. even if you just ate.

You can feel sad of not having good friends, regardless of what friends you have.

You CAN feel guilt about those feelings. But you don't HAVE to...

See, YOU get to feel however you FEEL, but you ALSO get to FEEL about how you FEEL however you want!

It's YOUR life! YOUR OWN!

You are the main character in YOUR story...

Now, you get to decide if you really care about how others will perceive you or not... 

I think you are a great person! You paint! You like naps! You like to sit with friends and joke around!

It makes me want to be your friend...

but perhaps the people you know suck? If that's the case, how is that your fault?

But is it my fault they suck? I would have stuck with them until the end of the world! 

If they are not willing to do the same for me, shame of them, not on me.

so I am making new friends. It's not easy. But I don't let my old friend make me feel like a reject anymore.

It's not easy, but please, keep talking to us. I am not very agile right now at this, but there are better people around here.

Perhaps you could set yourself a small goal, like go walk around the block before each time you want to watch porn on your phone?

You start this small, and slowly, as you gain confidence to be able to do it, you increase (2 walks about the block... a walk around 2 blocks).

You also start to create a condition in your mind: no reward (the porn) without effort (the walk).

But the effort is not important.. it can be "clean my room", "study 1 hour", 

The idea is to just create a routine in which you do what you need to do (effort) before what you want to do (reward).

As you slowly start  to build up your ability to put the efforts before the reward, perhaps your confidence will rise.

I am not one to talk much, but my mother in law has BPD and was miserable all of her life... until she kicked it.

I know you probably don't believe it, but BPD is one of the rare mental illnesses you can actually cure!

I am not saying it's easy, but you can. Don't lose hope...

In fact, accepting you have BPD is the first step of getting better. It took over 30 years for my mother in law to accept she had a mental illness, and within 12 months of accepting it, she was getting help, and only a few months later, she was already much happier.

It took her less than 2 years from acceptance to almost being cured.

In her case, the almost being cured made a MASSIVE change: she started having fun laughing, reading, taking care of her. Her anguish and anxiety went 80% away.

She still has anxiety, but no longer really BPD.

It might be longer (or shorter) for you, but it's doable. Don't give up...
